content: Tobramycin is classified as an aminoglycoside antibiotic. It is specifically used to treat bacterial eye infections and is ineffective against other types of eye infections. To apply the eye drops, first wash your hands thoroughly. Avoid wearing contact lenses while using this medication. Tilt your head back, look upward, and gently pull down the lower eyelid to create a small pouch. Hold the dropper directly above your eye and instill one drop into the pouch. After applying the drop, look downward and gently close your eyes for 1 to 2 minutes. Place one finger at the inner corner of your eye (near the nose) and apply gentle pressure to prevent the medication from draining out. Avoid blinking or rubbing your eyes. Do not rinse the dropper after use. If you are using other eye medications, such as drops or ointments, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before applying the next medication. Use this medication consistently to achieve the best results. To help you remember, administer the drops at the same times each day. Continue using the medication for the full duration prescribed, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include tearing, eye redness, discomfort, or itching/swelling of the eyelids. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to a new fungal eye infection. Do not use it for longer than prescribed. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before using tobramycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other aminoglycosides (e.g., gentamicin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as preservatives like benzalkonium chloride, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. After applying the medication, your vision may become temporarily blurred or unstable. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Discard any unused medication after completing the treatment. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Check the product packaging for specific instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
